title: Debojo Community Energy Campus
project_type: A community-scale energy development designed to provide reliable electricity through an integrated distributed-energy system.
operating_model:
Palm 11 through a power purchase agreement and working with partners will finance, build, own and run
 the energy system, while the customer buys the electricity Palm 11 produces at an agreed tariff. The customer pays for energy delivered, not for the equipment, so there's little or no upfront cost.
short_description: Palm 11 develops and integrates distributed energy systems combining solar, battery storage, hybrid generation and smart energy management to deliver reliable power where itis needed.
challenge:
When electricity disappears from a community for weeks or months, the damage goes far beyond darkness. Power underpins almost every part of daily life, and its absence slowly weakens a community's health, economy, and safety.

Schools
Without power, teaching suffers. Classrooms are dim, computers and projectors are unusable, and fans don't work in the heat. Students can't study after dark, so homework and exam preparation suffer. Schools also lose access to digital learning, and teachers may move to places with better conditions, leaving gaps in staff.

Businesses
Small businesses are hit hardest. Shops, salons, tailors, and workshops depend on electricity to operate. Many owners turn to generators, but fuel costs eat into profits, and some close entirely. Fewer customers and fewer sales mean lost jobs and falling household incomes, so the whole local economy shrinks.

Roads and safety
Streets without lighting become dangerous after dark. Accidents are more likely, and residents are more exposed to crime, so people stay indoors and trade stops early. Traffic lights fail at junctions, and emergency services struggle to move quickly and safely.

Food
Without refrigeration, food spoils quickly. Traders lose fresh produce, meat, and fish, and families can't store leftovers. Food becomes more expensive and less safe, and rising illness from spoiled food puts added pressure on clinics that may themselves have limited power.

Homes and family life
At home, families rely on candles, kerosene lamps, or costly generators, which bring fire risks and fumes. Phones can't be charged, so people lose contact with relatives and access to news. Water pumps stop, so households must fetch and carry water. Daily chores, cooking, and studying take longer and cost more.

Health and wellbeing
Clinics can't keep vaccines and medicines cold, and equipment stops working. Night-time births and emergencies become far riskier. Stress, poor sleep, and isolation also take their toll on mental health.

The long-term effect

Together, these problems keep a community poorer, less educated, and less healthy than it could be. Restoring a reliable power supply isn't a luxury. It's the foundation for stronger schools, healthier families, and a growing local economy.
palm11_solution:
Palm 11 will build a local microgrid that combines five elements, each covering the others' weaknesses:

1. Solar PV supplies low-cost daytime energy with no fuel bill.

2. Battery storage (BESS) keeps solar energy for the evening, covers short gaps instantly, and smooths out fluctuations.

3.Gas/CNG generation provides firm power at night, in cloudy spells, and at peak demand, and recharges the batteries when needed.

4. The grid connection supplies cheap energy when available and acts as a backup.

5. An energy management system (EMS) decides which source to use at each moment, protects the batteries, and shuts off non-essential loads first if supply is tight.

How it solves the problem

Schools: reliable lighting, fans, and computers, with evening study possible.

Businesses: steady power, with lower running costs than diesel, so shops and workshops stay open and grow.

Roads and safety: street lighting returns, improving safety and extending trading hours.

Food and health: refrigeration for traders, households, and clinics, so less food is wasted and medicines stay safe.

Homes: safe lighting, phone charging, and water pumping, replacing kerosene and noisy generators.

Resilience: if the grid fails, the system disconnects automatically and keeps the community powered.

Benefits
Lower long-term energy cost, since solar and efficient gas replace costly diesel

Cleaner, quieter operation with lower emissions

A system that can grow by adding panels, batteries, or engines

Local jobs in operation and maintenance
Implementation

Survey the community and measure its energy demand, with priority loads identified.
Size the solar, battery, and generator to that demand.

Secure a reliable CNG supply and the necessary permits.
Install and commission the system, with grid connection and protection.

Train local operators and set up monitoring and maintenance.
